first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are funnel-mechanics problems, and the inherited record points at simplification as the lever with durable rather than borrowed effects: memory_86 ties shortened onboarding to completion and time-to-value, memory_31 ties fewer signup fields to a durable first-week activation lift. Those two are the load-bearing claims for the action, so they are what I spend the verification budget on — I want the original records to confirm the effect was measured on retained/qualified accounts rather than raw funnel counts, and to see whether the day-12 and day-52 conditions resemble day 76. Promotional pricing is the tempting answer because the competitor pressure is priced, but memory_73 explicitly records that it bought acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it; against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching entry pricing converts a competitive problem into a churn problem and I decline it rather than re-litigate it with scarce analyst time. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the credible runner-up and would be my fallback if verification weakens the simplification record, but it addresses only one of the two declining metrics. Downstream risk flagged: cutting required signup fields removes qualification data, which can degrade the demo-request/sales-assisted path that memory_44 credits with better enterprise pipeline quality — so the test should preserve enterprise routing and instrument lead quality, not just completion rate. Uncertainty preserved: all supporting memories are 15-64 days old and consolidated summaries, the current declines may stem from competitor-driven mix shift rather than funnel friction (in which case a friction fix will underperform), and standard experiment scale with retention and qualified-revenue readouts is chosen over broad rollout precisely because a completion-rate lift is not yet evidence of a qualified-revenue lift.

final.rationale: Verification held. exp_86 is the strongest record in the inherited set: shortened onboarding lifted completion +13%, cut time-to-value 2.1 days, and — critically for a sustainable-revenue objective — moved 30-day retention +3%, so the gain is not borrowed from the back of the funnel. exp_31 is confirmed but narrower and weaker than its summary implied: activation +9% and qualified revenue +4%, but retention -1% and explicitly not replicated outside SMB. So I commit to simplify_onboarding, weighted toward the onboarding-shortening mechanism from exp_86 as the primary lever, with signup-field reduction as a secondary component scoped to SMB where it actually replicated. This directly attacks both declining metrics: onboarding completion -4% and, via time-to-value and first-week activation, the -6% activation drop. I continue to decline promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing; memory_73 records acquisition and revenue lift purchased with materially worse 30-day retention and carries an explicit do-not-generalize warning, and answering a price attack with a retention leak is the wrong trade against a long-term qualified-revenue objective. Competitive pressure is a real force but it argues for faster time-to-value, which is what exp_86 delivers. Downstream value risk flagged and unchanged by verification: cutting required signup fields strips qualification data that memory_44 credits for enterprise pipeline quality through the demo-request path, so enterprise routing stays intact, the field reduction is gated to the SMB path only, and lead quality is instrumented alongside completion. Uncertainty preserved rather than resolved: exp_31's -1% retention is small but the wrong sign and I will not assume it stays small at scale; the segment non-replication is a documented boundary, not noise; neither source record was run under competitor-pricing conditions, so the current declines may be mix shift rather than friction, in which case a friction fix underperforms its historical effect size. Standard experiment, not broad rollout — the archive confirmed a mechanism, not a guaranteed transfer to day-76 conditions. Readout is 30-day retention and qualified revenue by segment, not completion rate alone; broad rollout only if retention holds non-negative and qualified revenue moves.
